info.name: Jaeger(2024)
info.description: Jaeger class (5.5e / 2024 rules, v2.1.3) from Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt. Separate from the 2014 Steinhardt "Jaeger" class; both can be loaded together.

description.p: An unassuming human pounces in the night, his blade and revolver at the ready. A gunshot, followed by the sound of metal against flesh and the splattering of blood over cobblestone. He snickers before plunging his blade anew into his battered prey.
An elegant manikin vaults atop a maddened monster, before putting the barrel of her cannon against its skull and pulling the trigger. She had always loved explosions.
Battleaxe in hand, a massive orc brutally decapitates a beast, then leaps towards another, impaling the silvered weapon in the creature’s chest and ripping a gashing wound from neck to groin.

Jaegers are defined by their efficiency in battle, using their mastery over both steel and gunpowder to lay waste to all who oppose them. More than just soldiers, their skills represent the last wall of defense of a world fated to extinction; they are unstoppable and unbreakable. They strike fear in the heart of their foes, and bring hope to those they protect.

In the ease and safety that contemporary advancements bring, city dwellers frequently forget how fortunate their lives are. They have all but forgotten the life of pain that would befall them if the system failed. Which is precisely what took place in Luyarnha.

The urbanites were left defenseless when the scourge swept the streets of the city, snapping like twigs in the face of such ferocity. While the denizens of the town struggled against insurmountable odds, the church and the nobility didn’t remain inert, instead concentrating their efforts to engineer the ideal weapon, something capable of annihilating the beasts plaguing the city. This weapon came to be known as the jaegers.

Jaegers thrive in the savagery of the hunt. Their reflexes more honed than that of mere mortals, jaegers are capable of dodging the most vicious of blows and using that momentum to drive their blade deep into the heart of their prey. A jaeger’s thirst for battle is endless; only in inaction can they experience fatigue. They are the perfect weapon against the nightmarish tides of beasts and the sole reason Luyarnha still stands.

One who hunts beasts is a “hunter”, as they are commonly called by civilized society, but few hunters have the jaeger class. Coming from all walks of life, jaegers blend in with their communities, only unleashing their abilities in times of need. They act as guardians for people who are unable to defend themselves, and they serve as the bloody sword of vengeance in a world that is hell-bent on destroying itself. Life in the city-state of Luyarnha is fraught with peril: gang warfare, infectious madness, and harrowing beasts. Amidst this chaos, jaegers are the first to charge into battle so that their brothers and sisters can survive to live another day.

Jaegers rarely leave their home city of Luyarnha; they would rather die than see it fall to the scourge. Following the jaeger's creed—'survive together, or die together'—they never hunt by themselves unless forced to. The nights can be brutal and the beasts are relentless; against such a ferocious onslaught, only a united front can hope to survive. As a result, jaegers are aware of the importance of teamwork and never charge into battle alone, save to retrieve fallen allies. The bonds formed during the hunts are stronger than those of many families. Blood is thicker than water, and the gods know that blood is shed when the hunt rages on.

Think about the nature of your abilities and what gave rise to them as you construct your jaeger character. Were you one of the numerous orphans whose bodies were experimented on in the jaeger research project? Did you voluntarily join the ranks of hunters, or were you abducted and brainwashed into the ideal soldier? Alternatively, you might have defied the established order and joined the jaegers by a different route, perhaps after finding an eldritch carving and engraving it on your flesh. You might be self-taught—a loner who learned combat skills, tracking, or even a magical connection to the cosmos through the necessity of surviving the hunts. Alternatively, you might have learned from the comrades you now consider family.

What fuels you? Is it a visceral hatred of the beasts that slaughtered your loved ones? Or is it a reflection of your desire to stop these monsters' devastation, committing yourself to reining in their carnage? Is your adventuring career a continuation of your work in annihilating the scourge of beasts, or a significant change? What made you join a band of adventurers? Do you enjoy the break from the hunt that new allies provide, or do you find it difficult to teach them the jaeger ways?

ul.li: Primary Ability: Strength or Dexterity
Hit Point Die: D8 per Jaeger level
Saving Throw Proficiencies: Dexterity and Intelligence
Skill Proficiencies: Choose 2: Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, or Survival
Weapon Proficiencies: Simple and Martial weapons
Armor Training: Light and Medium armor and Shields

Starting Equipment: Choose A, B or C: (A) Handaxe, Cleaver, Blunderbuss, Pouch of 20 Bullets, Scale Mail, Explorer’s Pack, and 1 GP; (B) Rapier, Scythe, Pistol, Pouch of 20 Bullets, Leather Armor, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 29 GP; or (C) 115 GP

description.p: As a Level 1 Jaeger: Gain all the traits in the Core Jaeger Traits table. Gain the Jaeger’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Jaeger Features table.

As a Multiclass Jaeger: Gain the following traits from the Core Jaeger Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Martial weapons, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields. Gain the Jaeger’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Jaeger Features table.

tr.td: Adrenaline, Eldritch Hunter, Flexible Combatant, Weapon Mastery

description.p: As a Jaeger, you gain the following class features when you reach the specified Jaeger levels. These features are listed in the Jaeger Features table.

setters.set: A hunter of the Eldritch Hunt (2024 rules).
Martial weapons, Light armor, Medium armor, Shields

description.p: You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one, and you can reload weapons with the Loading, Reload, or Barrel properties without a free hand.

Additionally, if you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and a one-handed ranged weapon in the other, you do not have Disadvantage from being within 5 feet of an enemy on attacks made with that ranged weapon.

sheet.description: You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one, and you can reload weapons with the Loading, Reload, or Barrel properties without a free hand. While wielding a melee weapon in one hand and a one-handed ranged weapon in the other, you don't have Disadvantage on attacks with that ranged weapon from being within 5 feet of an enemy.

description.p: Your focus during battle is razor sharp, letting you keenly use Adrenaline during critical moments. You have 1 Adrenaline Point. You gain additional Adrenaline Points at Jaeger level 2, 5, 9, 13, and 17, as shown on the Jaeger table. You can expend Adrenaline Points to use Adrenaline Arts. You learn two such Adrenaline Arts: Weapon Parry and Dodge Step. You learn one additional Adrenaline Art of your choice at 2nd, 7th, 13th, and 17th level. Whenever you gain a Jaeger level, you can replace one of your Adrenaline Arts with another one. Your Adrenaline Art options are detailed at the end of the class description.

You regain all expended Adrenaline Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest. When you roll a 20 on a saving throw, or on an attack roll against an enemy, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point. When you roll Initiative and have no Adrenaline Points remaining, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: You have {{jaeger24:adrenaline points}} Adrenaline Points, regained on a Short or Long Rest. When you roll a 20 on a saving throw, or on an attack roll against an enemy, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point. When you roll Initiative with no Adrenaline Points remaining, you regain 1.

description.p: When you make an ability check to track or identify an Aberration, Celestial, Fiend, Monstrosity, or Undead, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the ability check. If you are already proficient in the ability check, you can double your Proficiency Bonus.

sheet.description: When you make an ability check to track or identify an Aberration, Celestial, Fiend, Monstrosity, or Undead, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the check. If you are already proficient, you double your Proficiency Bonus.

description.p: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

sheet.description: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change one of your two Weapon Mastery choices for a different one.

description.p: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose one of the options below.
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (such as Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, or Two-Weapon Fighting).

Flexible Fighting. When you attack with a weapon you are wielding in one hand, you can make an extra attack as a Bonus Action with a different weapon you are wielding in the other hand, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. You can't benefit from this feature if you've used the Nick Weapon Mastery this turn.
While wielding two weapons, you gain +1 to the damage rolls of both weapons.

sheet.description: When you attack with a weapon you are wielding in one hand, you can make an extra attack as a Bonus Action with a different weapon in your other hand (no ability modifier to its damage unless negative). Not usable if you used the Nick mastery this turn. While wielding two weapons, you gain +1 to the damage rolls of both weapons.

description.p: Focused Fighting. You learn an additional Adrenaline Art, and you gain 1 additional Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: You learn an additional Adrenaline Art, and you gain 1 additional Adrenaline Point.

description.p: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Adrenaline Points. When you do so, roll your Momentum Die and add it to your Initiative roll.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

sheet.description: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Adrenaline Points and add one roll of your Momentum Die (d{{jaeger24:momentum die}}) to the Initiative roll.

description.p: In combat, you can build up Momentum, a force that empowers your strikes and enables brutal finishing moves. While you have 1 or more Momentum dice, your Momentum follows the rules below.
Duration. Your Momentum dice last until the end of your next turn. If you still have Momentum dice at the start of your next turn, you can keep them for another round by doing one of the following:

ul.li: Gain a Momentum die.
Make an attack roll against a hostile creature.
End your turn within 5 feet of a hostile creature.

description.p: Each time your Momentum dice are sustained this way, they last until the end of your next turn.

Momentum Dice. Each time you expend an Adrenaline Point, you gain 1 Momentum die. Your Momentum die is a d6, and it increases as you gain Jaeger levels, as shown in the Jaeger Features table. You can hold a maximum number of Momentum dice equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (whichever is higher).

Finishers. You can expend all of your Momentum dice to execute a Finisher. You know the Brutal Finisher. You learn one additional Finisher of your choice when you reach Jaeger levels 4, 6, 8, and 12, and may gain others through Jaeger Chapter features. Whenever you gain a Jaeger level, you can replace one of your Finishers with another one.

div.p: Momentum functions similarly to a Barbarian’s Rage—as long as you meet one of the criteria, you keep all your Momentum dice until the end of your next turn. Did you gain a Momentum die? Did you attack a hostile creature? Did you end your turn within 5 feet of a hostile creature? If yes to any of these, keep your Momentum dice.
Whenever you ‘add the number of Momentum dice expended to damage’, roll the expended dice and add the total rolled to the damage, not the number of dice itself.

sheet.description: Each time you expend an Adrenaline Point, you gain 1 Momentum die (d{{jaeger24:momentum die}}, maximum {{jaeger24:momentum max}} dice). Dice last until the end of your next turn; sustain them by gaining a die, attacking a hostile creature, or ending your turn within 5 feet of one. Expend all Momentum dice to execute a Finisher.

description.p: You choose a Jaeger Chapter which reflects how you intend to further your powers. Select one of the following: Absolute Chapter, Heretic Chapter, Marauder Chapter, Salvation Chapter, or Sanguine Chapter.

You gain the ability to activate a magical sight at will (no action required), allowing you to effortlessly pierce the gloom and see what lurks within. For 1 hour, you gain Darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases to 120 feet. This vision lets you see normally in Dim Light and Darkness—both magical and nonmagical (such as the magical Darkness caused by the Darkness spell).

When you reach 7th level the Darkvision granted by this feature becomes permanent, but when activating the feature you gain the effect of See Invisibility for the duration. When you reach 13th level, you additionally gain the effect of True Seeing for the duration when activating the feature.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you complete a Long Rest.

sheet.description: For 1 hour, you gain Darkvision 60 ft. (120 ft. if you already have Darkvision) that sees through magical and nonmagical Darkness.

Your Darkvision from this feature is permanent (60 ft., or 120 ft. if you already had Darkvision), and sees through magical and nonmagical Darkness. When you activate this feature, you gain the effect of See Invisibility for 1 hour.

Your Darkvision from this feature is permanent (60 ft., or 120 ft. if you already had Darkvision), and sees through magical and nonmagical Darkness. When you activate this feature, you gain the effects of See Invisibility and True Seeing for 1 hour.

description.p: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Jaeger levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

You have Advantage on checks made to find secret passages, interpret markings or messages left by other creatures on walls or surfaces, or determine the fate of creatures from blood stains and remains.

sheet.description: You have Advantage on checks made to find secret passages, interpret markings or messages left by other creatures on walls or surfaces, or determine the fate of creatures from blood stains and remains.

description.p: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

sheet.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

description.p: At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to immediately move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

sheet.description: At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to immediately move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

description.p: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.
You don't benefit from this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

sheet.description: When an effect allows a Dexterity saving throw for half damage, you take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. Not while Incapacitated.

description.p: The first time you hit a creature on your turn, you gain 1 Momentum die. You gain 1 additional Momentum die any time you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points.

sheet.description: The first time you hit a creature on your turn, you gain 1 Momentum die. You gain 1 additional Momentum die any time you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points.

description.p: When you use your Hunter's Pursuit, if you end your movement next to a hostile creature, you regain the expended Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: When you use your Hunter's Pursuit, if you end your movement next to a hostile creature, you regain the expended Adrenaline Point.

description.p: You gain Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions, and against effects that cause Madness. If you fail a saving throw against any of these, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to reroll the die. You must use the new roll.

sheet.description: You have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions and against effects that cause Madness. If you fail one of these saves, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to reroll; you must use the new roll.

description.p: You are always under the effect of your Piercing Gaze.

sheet.description: You are always under the effect of your Piercing Gaze.

description.p: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Combat Prowess is recommended.

Once per round (beginning at the start of each of your turns), you gain one additional Reaction, which you can only use on an Adrenaline Art that requires a Reaction (such as Weapon Parry or Dodge Step). When you expend an Adrenaline Point on this special Reaction, you immediately regain the expended Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: Once per round (beginning at the start of each of your turns), you gain one additional Reaction usable only on an Adrenaline Art that requires a Reaction (such as Weapon Parry or Dodge Step). When you expend an Adrenaline Point on this special Reaction, you immediately regain it.

p.i: Jaegers of the Absolute Chapter aim for the perfect hunt: to kill their prey without suffering a single hit. Quick hands, quick feet, and quick minds, they never stay still—always one step ahead, always striking with lethal accuracy. They are masters of their craft, refining the core techniques of a jaeger to absolute perfection.

description.p: When you use the Weapon Parry Adrenaline Art, if you reduce the damage to 0, you can make a single weapon attack against the attacker if they are within Reach of a melee weapon you are wielding. If the target is Stunned as a result of your Weapon Parry Adrenaline Art, on a hit, this attack is a Critical Hit.
Whenever you expend an Adrenaline Point on an Adrenaline Art, you gain Advantage on your next weapon attack roll before the end of your next turn.

sheet.description: When Weapon Parry reduces the damage to 0, you can make one weapon attack against the attacker if it is within Reach of a melee weapon you are wielding; if it was Stunned by that Weapon Parry, a hit is a Critical Hit. Whenever you expend an Adrenaline Point on an Adrenaline Art, you have Advantage on your next weapon attack roll before the end of your next turn.

description.p: While you are wearing light armor or no armor, and are not wearing a shield, your Speed increases by 10 feet, Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage, and the distance you can move when using the Dodge Step Adrenaline Art increases by 5 feet.

sheet.description: While wearing light or no armor and no shield: your Speed increases by 10 feet, Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage, and Dodge Step moves you 5 extra feet.

description.p: Once per turn, if you move to the opposite side of a creature from where you started your turn, or are directly on the opposite side of a creature from an allied creature of yours, you deal extra damage to the target equal to your Momentum die the first time you hit it with a melee weapon attack, and you gain 1 Momentum die.

sheet.description: If you move to the opposite side of a creature from where you started your turn, or are directly opposite an ally across it, the first time you hit it with a melee weapon attack you deal extra damage equal to your Momentum die (d{{jaeger24:momentum die}}) and gain 1 Momentum die.

description.p: When you move as part of your Hunter's Pursuit feature, or Dodge Step and Jaeger’s Rush Adrenaline Arts, you ignore Difficult Terrain, can move through hostile creatures’ spaces, and have a Climb and Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

sheet.description: When you move with Hunter's Pursuit, Dodge Step or Jaeger’s Rush, you ignore Difficult Terrain, can move through hostile creatures’ spaces, and have a Climb and Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

description.p: You can declare a hunt (no action required). For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

ul.li: You are under the effect of Freedom of Movement.
Each time you expend an Adrenaline Point, you gain 2 Momentum dice instead of 1.
If you start your turn with no Adrenaline Points, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: This effect ends early if you become Incapacitated. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

sheet.description: For 1 minute: you are under the effect of Freedom of Movement; each Adrenaline Point you expend grants 2 Momentum dice instead of 1; if you start your turn with no Adrenaline Points, you regain 1. Ends early if you become Incapacitated.

p.i: The Heretic Chapter's jaegers are despised by both religious organizations and their adherents. In a world where acts of faith are required to harness divine powers, these jaegers instead rip these powers from the very gods, tearing away their divine fabric. Through blasphemous rituals, strange ingestions, and direct grafting of powers onto their flesh, heretics bind the powers of greater beings to their will. This is a path that calls for a certain madness that is only found in the most ardent of hunters, those who feel the burning need to reach the pinnacle of power and will do anything to achieve it. Some seek such power for its own sake, but most want it to put an end to the nightmare.

description.p: You bend dark powers to your service through blasphemous occult rituals, making them your own. You gain the ability to cast spells.
Cantrips. You learn two Cantrips of your choice from the Warlock spell list. You learn an additional Warlock Cantrip of your choice at level 10.

Spell Slots. The Heretic Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have, as well as the level of those spell slots. All of your spell slots are of the same level. To cast one of your Warlock spells of level 1 or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 spells from the Warlock spell list. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Jaeger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Heretic Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Warlock spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what’s shown in the table’s Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 7, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–2.
Changing your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Jaeger level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell for which you have spell slots.
Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.
Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus, or a Simple or Martial weapon as a Spellcasting Focus to cast spells from your Warlock spell list.

center.p: Spell save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier
Spell attack modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

sheet.description: You have {{warlock:spellcasting:slots:count}} spell slot(s) of level {{warlock:spellcasting:slot}}, regained on a Short or Long Rest. Whenever you gain a Jaeger level, you can replace one prepared spell with another Warlock spell for which you have slots. You can use an Arcane Focus or a Simple or Martial weapon as your Spellcasting Focus.

description.p: Eldritch Invocation. You learn one Eldritch Invocation of your choice from the Warlock's list of Eldritch Invocation Options. If an invocation refers to Charisma, you use your Intelligence instead.

At higher levels, you learn additional Eldritch Invocations, and your effective Warlock level for invocation prerequisites increases, as shown below. Whenever you gain a level in the Jaeger class, you can replace one Eldritch Invocation you know with another one for which you meet the prerequisites.

ul.li: Level 7: You learn one additional Eldritch Invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for invocation prerequisites.
Level 14: You learn one additional Eldritch Invocation. You are considered a level 5 Warlock for invocation prerequisites.
Level 17: You learn one additional Eldritch Invocation.

description.p: Spell Flurry. You also learn the Spell Flurry Adrenaline Art. This does not count against your total Adrenaline Arts known.

div.p: Aurora checks invocation prerequisites against your real Warlock level. To support the "considered a level 2 / level 5 Warlock" rule, this file includes Heretic copies ("Occult Art: ...") of the invocations that require Warlock level 2 or 5. They appear in your level 7, 14 and 17 invocation choices. Invocations without a level prerequisite (such as Pact of the Blade or Armor of Shadows) are chosen from the normal list.

select.name: Eldritch Invocation (Heretic 7)
select.supports: PHB24 Eldritch Invocation||Jaeger 2024 Occult Art W2

select.name: Eldritch Invocation (Heretic 14)
select.supports: PHB24 Eldritch Invocation||Jaeger 2024 Occult Art W2||Jaeger 2024 Occult Art W5

select.name: Eldritch Invocation (Heretic 17)
select.supports: PHB24 Eldritch Invocation||Jaeger 2024 Occult Art W2||Jaeger 2024 Occult Art W5

description.p: When you expend a spell slot from your Heretic Magic feature, you gain a number of Momentum dice equal to the level of the spell slot expended.

sheet.description: When you expend a spell slot from your Heretic Magic feature, you gain Momentum dice equal to the slot's level ({{warlock:spellcasting:slot}}).

description.p: When you use a Jaeger feature that allows you to move at least 5 feet (such as Chasing Finisher, Hunter's Pursuit or Jaeger’s Rush), you can teleport the distance moved instead.
When you do so for Dodge Step, you automatically succeed on the saving throw made to evade the attack.

sheet.description: When you use a Jaeger feature that moves you at least 5 feet (such as Chasing Finisher, Hunter's Pursuit or Jaeger’s Rush), you can teleport the distance instead. When you do so for Dodge Step, you automatically succeed on its saving throw.

description.p: You can unleash the twisted powers you've bound to your soul as a Bonus Action. For 1 minute, you become wreathed in darkness. You gain the following effects:

ul.li: The area in a 10-foot Emanation centered on you dims. Bright Light becomes Dim Light, and Dim Light becomes Darkness.
You are heavily obscured by swirling shadows.
You gain a Fly Speed of 30 feet.
You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Whenever you take Radiant damage you lose these Resistances until the start of your next turn.

description.p: These effects end early if you become Incapacitated. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you complete a Short or Long Rest.

sheet.description: For 1 minute: a 10-foot Emanation around you dims (Bright→Dim, Dim→Darkness); you are Heavily Obscured; you gain a Fly Speed of 30 feet; you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage (lost until the start of your next turn whenever you take Radiant damage). Ends early if you become Incapacitated.

p.i: A jaeger of the Marauder Chapter embodies raw slaughter. Vengeance, wrath, and death, all rolled into one swing that never ceases, endlessly cleaving through monsters, leaving a bloody wake of destruction. Each marauder is a symbol of the Chapter's determination and savagery, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies with their every swing. They are unstoppable warriors, driven by a thirst for vengeance and the need to protect humanity from the monstrous hordes.

description.p: You learn the Great Cleave Finisher. This does not count against your Finishers known.
While you are wielding a melee weapon with the Two-Handed property, the size of your Momentum die is increased by one step (from a d6 to a d8, to a d10 at 11th level, and to a d12 at 17th level).

sheet.description: While wielding a melee weapon with the Two-Handed property, your Momentum die is d{{jaeger24:marauder momentum die}} instead of d{{jaeger24:momentum die}}.

description.p: You wade through your enemies relying on your toughness and grit. Your Hit Point Maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Jaeger level.
While you are wearing Medium Armor, you can add your Constitution modifier (to a maximum of +2) instead of your Dexterity modifier to determine your Armor Class.

sheet.description: Your Hit Point Maximum increases by 3, +1 per Jaeger level after 3rd. While wearing Medium Armor, you can use your Constitution modifier (max +2) instead of your Dexterity modifier for your Armor Class.

description.p: Once per turn, if you move more than 15 feet toward a creature (or fall 10 feet or more) immediately before making a weapon attack against them, you deal extra damage on a hit equal to your Momentum die and you gain 1 Momentum die.

When falling, you can make this attack prior to hitting the ground if there is a creature in the space where you would fall. On a hit, any damage you would take as a result of falling is reduced by half, and you do not fall Prone from the fall.

sheet.description: If you move more than 15 feet toward a creature (or fall 10+ feet) immediately before a weapon attack against it, a hit deals extra damage equal to your Momentum die and you gain 1 Momentum die. When falling onto a creature, you can attack before landing; on a hit, falling damage is halved and you don't fall Prone.

description.p: When you use a Finisher you can force one target hit by the Finisher to succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus + the number of Momentum Die expended) or be knocked Prone. Creatures that are Large or larger have Disadvantage on this saving throw.
If you use the Great Cleave Finisher, you can instead force all creatures damaged by the Finisher to make this saving throw.

div.p: You add the number of dice itself to the DC, you do not roll them and add that total to the DC.

sheet.description: When you use a Finisher, one target hit by it must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC {{jaeger24:fell the leviathan:dc}} + number of Momentum dice expended) or be knocked Prone; Large or larger creatures have Disadvantage. With Great Cleave, all creatures damaged by it make this save.

description.p: Your strength is so great that you can wield a two-handed weapon in one hand, and while you are wielding a weapon in one hand, it is treated as having the Light weapon property.
If you use two hands to wield a two-handed weapon, your attacks with it deal extra damage equal to half your Strength modifier (rounded up) on a hit.

Additionally, when you use a Finisher, you can double the number of Momentum dice you have (to no more than your maximum Momentum dice + 1). Once you've doubled your dice, you can't do so again until you complete a Short or Long Rest, or use your Jaeger’s Surge feature.

sheet.description: You can wield a two-handed weapon in one hand, and a weapon wielded in one hand counts as Light. Wielding a two-handed weapon in two hands, its hits deal extra damage equal to half your Strength modifier (rounded up). When you use a Finisher, you can double your Momentum dice (max {{jaeger24:momentum max}} + 1); recharges on a Short or Long Rest or when you use Jaeger’s Surge.

p.i: A divine force endows jaegers of the Salvation Chapter with the ability to defend the world from horrors, purging evil with one hand while saving the innocent with the other. Favorites of the Radiant Church, they are the light of hope in the darkness where evil dwells. Members of the Salvation Chapter know that prevention is always better than cure, and that murder is the most effective method of prevention. In their zealous righteousness, they offer hope of sanity and sanctuary to those that stand with them in their war against the monsters that plague Luyarnha.

description.p: You learn the Prayer of Salvation Adrenaline Art. This does not count against your Adrenaline Arts known.

You find new strength in the most desperate hours. When an allied creature you can see or hear is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again for 1 minute.

sheet.description: When an allied creature you can see or hear is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point. Once used, you can't do so again for 1 minute.

description.p: When you expend an Adrenaline Point, you can choose to emit a glow of divine light until the end of your next turn. The area in a 20-foot Emanation centered on you is Bright Light, and Dim Light an additional 20 feet beyond that. The light is Sunlight. Any allied creature that enters the Bright Light for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there gains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Momentum die. This light is extinguished early if you become Incapacitated.

sheet.description: When you expend an Adrenaline Point, you can emit Sunlight until the end of your next turn: Bright Light in a 20-foot Emanation and Dim Light 20 feet beyond. An ally that enters the Bright Light for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there regains 1d{{jaeger24:momentum die}} Hit Points. Ends early if you become Incapacitated.

description.p: Your Prayer of Salvation Adrenaline Art can target an additional creature, and the number of Hit Points it restores and Temporary Hit Points it grants increases to two rolls of your Momentum die.

The prayer also cleanses mind and body. When you use it, you can also end one Short-Term Madness or one of the following conditions affecting one of the creatures you heal: Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned.

sheet.description: Prayer of Salvation targets one additional creature and heals (and grants Temporary Hit Points equal to) 2d{{jaeger24:momentum die}}. When you use it, you can also end one Short-Term Madness or the Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned condition on one creature you heal.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you can unleash a blinding light from within for 1 minute, illuminating the darkness. You gain the following benefits for the duration:

ul.li: The Emanation of your Sanctifying Light increases to 30 feet of Bright Light and 30 feet of Dim Light beyond it. Each creature of your choice (including yourself) within the Bright Light is under the effect of Bless.

When you use Prayer of Salvation, choose one target other than yourself. Instead of rolling the Momentum dice to determine how many Hit Points that target regains, use the highest number possible for each die. The target also gains an equal number of Temporary Hit Points. You and any other targets of the Adrenaline Art roll the dice as normal.
When you use Prayer of Salvation, you immediately regain the expended Adrenaline Point.

description.p: These effects end early if you become Incapacitated. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you complete a Short or Long Rest.

sheet.description: For 1 minute: Sanctifying Light becomes 30 ft. Bright + 30 ft. Dim, and creatures of your choice in the Bright Light are under the effect of Bless; when you use Prayer of Salvation, one target other than you gets the maximum of each die (and equal Temporary Hit Points), and you regain the expended Adrenaline Point. Ends early if you become Incapacitated.

p.i: In order to strengthen themselves, jaegers of the Sanguine Chapter rely on the mastery of blood. They achieve resilient states of unnatural life and feed their powers with the fruits of their violence. Although some consider them to be monsters, when faced with the horrors of the Scourge, the sentiment quickly changes. These jaeger's abilities can hold the line and preserve the tenuous flame of life when it should have long since been extinguished, keeping themselves and their allies alive while draining the strength of their enemies in an endless crimson parade of blood.

description.p: You gain the ability to draw power from the flowing blood of your foes. You learn the Blood Drain Finisher, which does not count against your Finishers known.
Some of your abilities use a Sanguine save DC, which is calculated as follows:

center.p: Sanguine save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence or Constitution modifier (your choice)

sheet.description: Your Sanguine save DC is {{jaeger24:sanguine:dc}}.

description.p: You use Intelligence for your Sanguine save DC.
You use Constitution for your Sanguine save DC.
When you become Bloodied, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point and gain 1 Momentum die. You cannot benefit from this feature again for 1 minute.

sheet.description: When you become Bloodied, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point and gain 1 Momentum die. You can't benefit from this feature again for 1 minute.

description.p: When you use a Finisher against a target with the Bloodied condition, you can force one target hit by the Finisher to make a Constitution saving throw against your Sanguine save DC, selecting one of the following effects.

ul.li: Blood Puppet. The target must use its Reaction to move up to 5 feet in a direction of your choice, potentially provoking Opportunity Attacks. If the target's Reaction is unavailable, Blood Puppet fails.
Bound Blood. The target's Speed is halved until the start of your next turn.
Burning (Blood Drain Only). At the start of its next turn, the target takes Fire damage equal to half the Necrotic damage dealt.

description.p: You can choose one of these effects when using your Blood Drain Finisher even if the target does not have the Bloodied condition, and when using that Finisher it uses the Finisher's saving throw rather than making a separate saving throw.

sheet.description: When you use a Finisher against a Bloodied target, one target hit must make a Constitution save (DC {{jaeger24:sanguine:dc}}) or suffer one hex: Blood Puppet (uses its Reaction to move 5 ft. in a direction you choose; fails if no Reaction), Bound Blood (Speed halved until the start of your next turn), or Burning (Blood Drain only; Fire damage equal to half the Necrotic damage at the start of its next turn). Blood Drain can apply a hex to any target, using its own saving throw.

description.p: You can invoke more powerful blood hexes. You gain the following options for your Blood Hex feature, each of which can replace the hexes granted by Blood Hex, at the cost of 2 Adrenaline Points.
Blood Puppet (Empowered). The target must use its Reaction to move up to 10 feet and make a single weapon attack against a creature of your choice.

sheet.description: Empowered Blood Hex: the target must use its Reaction to move up to 10 feet and make a single weapon attack against a creature of your choice.

description.p: Bound Blood (Empowered). The target gains the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn.

sheet.description: Empowered Blood Hex: the target has the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn.

description.p: Burning Blood (Empowered). At the start of each of its turns, the target takes Fire damage equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. The target can make a Constitution saving throw against your Sanguine save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

sheet.description: Empowered Blood Hex: at the start of each of its turns, the target takes Fire damage equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. It repeats a Constitution save (DC {{jaeger24:sanguine:dc}}) at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

description.p: While you have the Bloodied condition you gain the following benefits:

ul.li: Your weapon attacks deal additional Necrotic damage equal to your Constitution or Intelligence modifier (your choice).
You have Resistance to Necrotic damage and Necrotic damage you deal ignores Resistance.

All Hit Points you regain from your Jaeger abilities are doubled. If an ability would restore you to no longer having the Bloodied condition, the effects of this ability do not fade until the end of your turn.
You can use the Blood Craze Adrenaline Art.

sheet.description: While Bloodied: your weapon attacks deal extra Necrotic damage equal to your Constitution or Intelligence modifier (your choice); you have Resistance to Necrotic damage and your Necrotic damage ignores Resistance; Hit Points you regain from Jaeger abilities are doubled (effects last until the end of your turn if healing ends Bloodied); you can use Blood Craze.

description.p: As a Reaction to being hit by an attack from a creature you can see within Reach or range of a weapon you are holding, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to reduce the attack's damage. The reduction equals one roll of your weapon's damage dice plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) and your Jaeger level.

If you roll the maximum amount of the weapon's damage die and reduce the damage to 0, you can force the attacker to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity or Strength modifier, whichever is higher). On a failed save, the target has the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn.

sheet.description: When hit by an attack from a creature you can see within Reach or range of a weapon you hold, reduce the damage by one roll of the weapon's damage dice + your Str or Dex modifier + {{jaeger24:level}}. If the weapon die rolls its maximum and the damage is reduced to 0, the attacker makes a Constitution save (DC {{jaeger24:dc}}) or is Stunned until the start of your next turn.

description.p: When an attack roll hits you, if your Speed is not 0, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to take a Reaction moving 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks and making a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to the attacker's attack roll (including modifiers). On a success, you evade completely and take no damage. On a failure, you halve the attack's damage against you.

sheet.description: When an attack roll hits you and your Speed isn't 0, move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks and make a Dexterity save (DC = the attack roll total). Success: no damage. Failure: half damage.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you expend 1 Adrenaline Point. You and one creature of your choice you can see within 60 feet of you each regain Hit Points equal to one roll of your Momentum die, and gain an equal number of Temporary Hit Points.

sheet.description: You and one creature you can see within 60 feet each regain 1d{{jaeger24:momentum die}} Hit Points and gain an equal number of Temporary Hit Points.

description.p: As a Reaction to being reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to fall to 1 Hit Point instead.

div.p: This is an Adrenaline Art, so it works with Always Ready (which grants an additional Reaction), making the Sanguine Chapter fairly difficult to stop at 20th level.

sheet.description: While Bloodied (Blood Frenzy), when you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you fall to 1 Hit Point instead.

description.p: When you cast a Cantrip or a spell of 1st level or higher, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to make a single weapon attack as a Bonus Action.

sheet.description: When you cast a Cantrip or a spell of 1st level or higher, you can make a single weapon attack as a Bonus Action.

description.p: Once per turn on your turn, when you make a jump, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to double your jumping distance for that jump, and you can ignore Difficult Terrain until the end of your turn. When you use this Adrenaline Art, the maximum distance you can jump isn’t limited by your Speed.

sheet.description: Once per turn on your turn, when you jump, double the jump's distance (not limited by your Speed) and ignore Difficult Terrain until the end of your turn.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you expend 1 Adrenaline Point and touch a weapon you're carrying. Choose between Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning. For 1 minute, the weapon deals that damage type instead of its normal type.

Once per turn on your turn, when you hit with an attack using this weapon, you deal additional damage equal to one roll of your Momentum Die. The damage is the same type as the one chosen for the weapon.

sheet.description: Touch a weapon you're carrying: for 1 minute it deals Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage (your choice) instead of its normal type, and once per turn on your turn a hit with it deals an extra 1d{{jaeger24:momentum die}} damage of that type.

description.p: As a Reaction to making a saving throw against the Charmed or Frightened conditions, or having your mind read or influenced, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to gain Advantage on the roll. If you already have Advantage on the roll, you can reroll one of the dice once.

sheet.description: When you make a saving throw against the Charmed or Frightened conditions, or against having your mind read or influenced, gain Advantage on it. If you already have Advantage, you can reroll one of the dice once.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point and gain 1 additional Momentum die (gaining 2 Momentum dice in total, which includes the die gained through the Momentum feature from expending the Adrenaline Point on Flourish).

sheet.description: Gain 1 additional Momentum die (2 Momentum dice in total, including the die gained from expending the Adrenaline Point).

element.name: I Don't Want To Be Eaten Today

description.p: As a Reaction to gaining the Grappled or Restrained conditions from an effect that has an escape DC or saving throw to end the effect early, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to attempt to immediately escape the effect, making an Athletics or Acrobatics check against the escape DC or saving throw DC.

sheet.description: When you gain the Grappled or Restrained condition from an effect with an escape DC or a saving throw to end it, immediately attempt to escape with an Athletics or Acrobatics check against that DC.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to take the Dash action.

sheet.description: Take the Dash action.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you can expend 1 Adrenaline Point to make an Investigation check against a creature you can see within 60 feet of you, contested by its Deception check. On success, you learn its creature type, AC, any damage Resistances, Immunities, or Vulnerabilities it has, and any spells currently affecting it.
Alternatively, when you take this Bonus Action, you can take the Search action.

sheet.description: Make an Investigation check contested by the Deception of a creature you can see within 60 feet. On a success, learn its creature type, AC, damage Resistances, Immunities and Vulnerabilities, and any spells affecting it. Alternatively, take the Search action.

description.p: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend all of your Momentum dice and add them to the damage roll. If you reduce the target to 0 Hit Points with this Finisher, or the target is reduced to 0 Hit Points before the start of your next turn, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: When you hit a creature with an attack, expend all Momentum dice and add them to the damage. If the target drops to 0 Hit Points from this Finisher or before the start of your next turn, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: When you hit a creature with an attack using a melee weapon with the Two-Handed property, you can expend all of your Momentum dice. When you do so, the attack’s Reach increases to 10 feet and it deals extra damage equal to 1 Momentum die to the target, and you cleave a number of adjacent targets within Reach equal to the number of dice expended. Make a melee weapon attack against each creature targeted. You regain 1 Adrenaline Point for each creature this reduces to 0 Hit Points, up to your maximum number of Adrenaline Points.

sheet.description: When you hit with a Two-Handed melee weapon, expend all Momentum dice: the attack's Reach becomes 10 feet, it deals 1 extra Momentum die of damage, and you make a melee weapon attack against a number of adjacent creatures within Reach equal to the dice expended. Regain 1 Adrenaline Point for each creature reduced to 0 Hit Points (up to your maximum).

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you expend all of your Momentum dice to drain the blood of a creature within 15 feet of you, consuming its vitality to empower you. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. Roll all of your expended Momentum dice, on a failed save the target takes Necrotic damage equal to the total rolled, or half as much on a successful save. Success or failure, you regain Hit Points equal to half the Necrotic damage dealt. If this would restore you above your Hit Point maximum, you gain the excess as Temporary Hit Points.

If the target has the Bloodied condition or is otherwise bleeding from an ability (such as the Hemorrhaging Wound finisher), it has Disadvantage on this saving throw, and you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: Expend all Momentum dice: a creature within 15 feet makes a Constitution save (DC {{jaeger24:sanguine:dc}}), taking Necrotic damage equal to the dice rolled on a failure or half on a success. You regain Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt (excess becomes Temporary Hit Points). Against a Bloodied or bleeding target, it has Disadvantage on the save and you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend all of your Momentum dice to force the target to make a saving throw, suffering a condition for 1 minute on a failure. The DC of the save is 8 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) + your Proficiency Bonus. The type of saving throw and the condition depend on the number of Momentum dice you have when you use this Finisher. You can choose to inflict a condition that requires fewer Momentum dice than you expend, but all Momentum dice are expended regardless of the condition selected.

The target can repeat its saving throw against the condition at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. If the condition inflicted is Prone, they do not need to pass a subsequent save and can end the condition by standing as normal instead. If the target fails its initial save against the effect, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: When you hit, expend all Momentum dice: the target saves (DC {{jaeger24:dc}}) or suffers a condition for 1 minute (repeat save at the end of each of its turns). 1 die: Str/Prone, 2: Con/Blinded, 3: Str/Restrained, 4: Con/Stunned, 5+: Con/Paralyzed. If it fails the initial save, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you expend all of your Momentum dice to move 10 feet per die expended before making a melee attack. This movement can be in any direction, including straight up. If nothing is holding you aloft after this attack, you fall. On a hit, add the expended Momentum dice to the attack’s damage roll, and until the end of the target’s next turn, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet per die expended.
If you move at least 30 feet using the Finisher, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: Expend all Momentum dice to move 10 feet per die (any direction, even straight up; you fall afterwards if nothing holds you aloft), then make a melee attack. On a hit, add the dice to the damage and reduce the target's Speed by 10 feet per die until the end of its next turn. Moving 30+ feet regains 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend all of your Momentum dice to rend a vicious bleeding wound. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it loses Hit Points equal to the Momentum dice expended. Each time it takes damage from this effect, the number of dice of damage it takes at the end of its next turn is reduced by 2, and the bleeding stops when the number of dice would be reduced to 0.

Applying a new bleed while the target is still bleeding does not stack, but instead refreshes the number of dice of damage taken from the bleed to the higher of the two values. This bleeding lasts for 1 minute or until the target regains Hit Points.
If a creature is slain while bleeding from this effect, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: When you hit, expend all Momentum dice: at the end of each of the target's turns it loses Hit Points equal to the dice, then the dice are reduced by 2 (stops at 0). New bleeds don't stack (use the higher). Lasts 1 minute or until it regains Hit Points. If it dies while bleeding, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: As a Reaction when a creature within 30 feet of you becomes Paralyzed, Restrained, or Stunned, you can expend all of your Momentum dice and make a single weapon attack against it with a ranged weapon you are holding. On a hit, the target takes damage equal to the weapon's damage roll plus the expended Momentum dice, you can inflict the Prone condition on the target, and you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: When a creature within 30 feet becomes Paralyzed, Restrained, or Stunned, expend all Momentum dice and make one attack against it with a ranged weapon you hold. On a hit: weapon damage + the dice, you can knock it Prone, and you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: As a Bonus Action, you expend all of your Momentum dice to warp your hand into a beast claw and make a melee weapon attack with it against a creature within 5 feet of you. You can use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls of this attack. On a hit, the target takes Slashing damage equal to 1d12 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier + the Momentum dice expended. This attack has a higher Critical Hit range based on the number of Momentum dice expended, reducing the roll needed by 1 for each die, up to a maximum of scoring a Critical Hit on a 10-20 with 10 Momentum dice.
If the Finisher is a Critical Hit, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: Expend all Momentum dice to make a beast-claw melee weapon attack (Str or Dex) against a creature within 5 feet: 1d12 + Str or Dex modifier + the dice in Slashing damage. Its Critical Hit range improves by 1 per die expended (up to 10–20 with 10 dice). On a Critical Hit, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

description.p: As a Bonus Action while you are holding a ranged weapon, you can expend all of your Momentum dice to fire a spray of shots at blinding speed. Each creature in a 30-foot Cone must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus). On a failure, a creature takes Piercing damage equal to the Momentum dice expended.
If the Finisher damages 2 or more creatures, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

sheet.description: While holding a ranged weapon, expend all Momentum dice: each creature in a 30-foot Cone makes a Dexterity save (DC {{jaeger24:volley finisher:dc}}), taking Piercing damage equal to the dice on a failure. If it damages 2 or more creatures, you regain 1 Adrenaline Point.

element.name: Occult Art: Agonizing Blast
element.prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage (Heretic Jaeger: level 7+)

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

p.em: Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage

description.p: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell’s damage rolls.
Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

sheet.description: {{agonizing blast:count}} of your cantrips, chosen when you gain this Invocation, gain +{{intelligence:modifier}} bonus to damage.

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

sheet.description: You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

element.name: Occult Art: Eldritch Spear
element.prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage and has a Range of 10+ Feet (Heretic Jaeger: level 7+)

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

p.em: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage

description.p: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level.
Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

sheet.description: {{eldritch spear:count}} of your cantrips, chosen when you gain this Invocation, gain extra 30 × your effective Warlock level ft. of range.

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell with this feature, you don’t roll the die for the Temporary Hit Points; you automatically get the highest number on the die.

sheet.description: You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot, and you always gain the maximum amount of THPs possible when casting the spell in this way.

element.name: Occult Art: Mask of Many Faces

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can cast Disguise Self without expending a spell slot.

sheet.description: You can cast Disguise Self without expending a spell slot.

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can cast Silent Image without expending a spell slot.

sheet.description: You can cast Silent Image without expending a spell slot.

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can cast Jump on yourself without expending a spell slot.

sheet.description: You can cast Jump on yourself without expending a spell slot.

element.name: Occult Art: Repelling Blast
element.prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage via an Attack Roll (Heretic Jaeger: level 7+)

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 2 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

p.em: Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage via an Attack Roll

description.p: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that requires an attack roll. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you.
Repeatable. You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

sheet.description: {{repelling blast:count}} of your cantrips, chosen when you gain this Invocation, gain ability to push Large or smaller creatures up to 10ft. straight away from you on hit.

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 5 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can cast Levitate on yourself without expending a spell slot.

sheet.description: You can cast Levitate on yourself without expending a spell slot.

element.name: Occult Art: Eldritch Smite
element.prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Blade (Heretic Jaeger: level 14+)

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 5 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

p.em: Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Blade

description.p: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra 1d8 Force damage to the target, plus another 1d8 per level of the spell slot, and you can give the target the Prone condition if it is Huge or smaller.

sheet.description: When you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra {{eldritch smite:damage}}d8 Force damage and give the target the Prone condition if it is Huge or smaller.

element.name: Occult Art: Gaze of Two Minds

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 5 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can use a Bonus Action to touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can take a Bonus Action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. The connection ends if you don’t maintain it in this way.

While perceiving through the other creature’s senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you can cast spells as if you were in your space or the other creature’s space if the two of you are within 60 feet of each other.

sheet.description: You can touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can take a Bonus Action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. The connection ends if you don’t maintain it in this way. While perceiving through the other creature’s senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you can cast spells as if you were in your space or the other creature’s space if the two of you are within 60 feet of each other.

element.name: Occult Art: Gift of the Depths

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 5 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

description.p: You can breathe underwater, and you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
You can also cast Water Breathing once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way again when you finish a Long Rest.

sheet.description: You can cast Water Breathing without expending a spell slot. Additionally, you can breathe underwater.

element.name: Occult Art: Investment of the Chain Master
element.prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Chain Invocation (Heretic Jaeger: level 14+)

p.i: Occult Arts (Heretic Chapter) copy of the Player’s Handbook (2024) invocation. You are considered a level 5 Warlock for its prerequisites; if it refers to Charisma, use Intelligence instead.

p.em: Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Chain Invocation

description.p: When you cast Find Familiar, you infuse the summoned familiar with a measure of your eldritch power, granting the creature the following benefits.
Aerial or Aquatic. The familiar gains either a Fly Speed or a Swim Speed (your choice) of 40 feet.
Quick Attack. As a Bonus Action, you can command the familiar to take the Attack action.
Necrotic or Radiant Damage. Whenever the familiar deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can make it deal Necrotic or Radiant damage instead.
Your Save DC. If the familiar forces a creature to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.
Resistance. When the familiar takes damage, you can take a Reaction to grant it Resistance against that damage.
